newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian Metals - Japan quiet, aluminium talks eyed.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Japan quiet, aluminium talks eyed.

text.p: Japan's physical metal markets have held quietly steady in the past week as the summer holidays draw to a close, while the focus in the aluminium market has been on two sets of negotiations under way in Tokyo, traders said.
Japanese trade houses continued last week's discussions of fourth-quarter aluminium premiums with Western producers.
Although few deals were thought to have been completed so far, trade sources reported talk that premiums were being set around $62 a tonne over London Metal Exchange cash prices.
Also scheduled for this week are talks between Venezuelan officials and the Japanese minority shareholders in Venezuela's 430,000-tonne-per-year capacity Venalum refinery.

The Venezuelan government hopes to resolve an ongoing dispute with the Japanese, who own 20 percent of the facility, as it seeks to privatise the country's aluminium sector by as early as the end of this year.
A delegation led by Venezuelan Investment Fund President Alberto Poletto arrived in Tokyo on Sunday and is scheduled to meet the Japanese consortium on Tuesday and Wednesday, industry sources said.
Poletto said in a statement on Friday that Venezuela had no intention of threatening to expropriate Japan's holdings, as suggested by Venezuelan press reports.

Venalum also recently resumed, at least for the time being, its 90,000-tonne-per-year equity shipments to Japan, which were suspended in February in an effort to pressure the Japanese to relinquish veto powers over Venalum decisions.

Japanese trade and industry sources remained wary about the chances for a near-term resolution to the squabble. "I have absolutely no idea (about the chances for a settlement)," said a source close to the Japanese consortium.

The physical copper market remained relatively tight, with premiums holding steady in light late-summer dealings, although an easing of premiums recently in Southeast Asia may work its way into the Japanese market as well, traders said.
Activity in the spot zinc market remained quiet and premiums held steady, although one trader said the market was closely monitoring the recent rise in U.S. premiums.
